stem: Timmy is an 8-month-old boy with episodic inconsolable crying, vomiting, and red currant jelly-like stool, suggesting intussusception. Which one of the following ultrasound findings would NOT be consistent with intussusception?
explanation: The double bubble sign is classically associated with duodenal obstruction, not intussusception. Target sign, doughnut sign, crescent in a doughnut sign, and pseudokidney sign are all described with intussusception on ultrasound.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Abdominal pain

rationale: The question asks for the finding NOT consistent with intussusception. Among the listed options, only the double bubble sign points to a different diagnosis.

optionExplanations.A: Consistent with intussusception; reflects the concentric bowel-within-bowel appearance.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect for intussusception; suggests duodenal obstruction rather than telescoping bowel.
optionExplanations.C: Consistent with intussusception; another descriptive ultrasound term for the target appearance.
optionExplanations.D: Consistent with intussusception; describes echogenic crescentic mesenteric fat within the lesion.
optionExplanations.E: Consistent with intussusception; a longitudinal ultrasound appearance of the intussuscepted bowel.

You have arranged for an abdominal ultrasound for Timmy. Which one of the following findings would NOT be consistent with your provisional diagnosis of intussusception?

Target sign

The following text applies to the questions at positions 8, 9, 10, 11, 12

Clinical Scenario 2 - Timmy

Next, you are taking a more detailed history about eight month old Timmy. He has a one day history of screaming inconsolably and poor feeding. He has also vomited breast milk twice over the past few hours. His mother has not measured any fever; there is no diarrhoea and no cold symptoms. When Timmy’s mother last changed the nappy, she noted some 'red currant jelly-like' substance. She has noted that between bouts of screaming, Timmy has been calm and at times quite sleepy.

The following five questions refer to Timmy’s clinical scenario.
